name: 克里斯托弗·哥伦布

points.title: 早年航海启蒙
points.description: 克里斯托弗·哥伦布出生于热那亚共和国的一个纺织工人家庭。年轻时，他跟随父亲学习编织，但很快对航海产生了浓厚兴趣。这一时期，他开始学习航海技术、绘制地图和拉丁语，并随商船在地中海地区航行。1473年左右，他成为了一名见习水手，参与了前往基克拉泽斯群岛和塞浦路斯的航行。这些早期经历为他后来的远航奠定了基础，培养了他对海洋的熟悉和对东方贸易路线的兴趣。
points.descriptionEn: Christopher Columbus was born in Genoa to a family of weavers. As a young man, he initially followed his father in the textile trade but quickly developed a passion for maritime activities. During this period, he learned navigation techniques, map-making, and Latin, and sailed on merchant ships throughout the Mediterranean. Around 1473, he became an apprentice seaman, participating in voyages to the Cyclades and Cyprus. These early experiences laid the foundation for his later expeditions, fostering his familiarity with the sea and his interest in trade routes to the East.

points.title: 寻求赞助与理论形成
points.description: 1476年，哥伦布的商船在葡萄牙海岸遭到法国海盗袭击后，他游到岸边并最终定居在里斯本。葡萄牙当时是欧洲航海技术的领先国家，哥伦布在这里学习了最新的航海知识，并参与了前往冰岛、几内亚和黄金海岸的航行。他研究了托斯卡内利等学者的著作，形成了向西航行到达亚洲的理论。1484年，他向葡萄牙国王约翰二世提出了西航计划，但遭到拒绝。这一时期，哥伦布完善了他的航海理论，并开始寻求其他赞助者。
points.descriptionEn: In 1476, after his merchant ship was attacked by French privateers off the Portuguese coast, Columbus swam ashore and eventually settled in Lisbon. Portugal was then a leader in maritime technology, and Columbus learned the latest navigation techniques there, participating in voyages to Iceland, Guinea, and the Gold Coast. He studied the works of scholars like Paolo dal Pozzo Toscanelli and developed his theory of sailing west to reach Asia. In 1484, he presented his westward voyage plan to King John II of Portugal, but it was rejected. During this period, Columbus refined his navigational theories and began seeking other patrons.

points.title: 首次横渡大西洋
points.description: 1492年8月3日，在西班牙女王伊莎贝拉一世的资助下，哥伦布率领三艘船（圣玛利亚号、平塔号和尼尼亚号）从帕洛斯港出发，开始了他的第一次远航。经过两个多月的航行，10月12日，他抵达了巴哈马群岛中的一个岛屿，并将其命名为圣萨尔瓦多。他误以为到达了亚洲，称当地居民为'印第安人'。随后他探索了古巴、海地等岛屿，建立了第一个殖民地纳维达德。1493年3月15日，他返回西班牙，向国王和王后报告了他的发现，开启了欧洲对美洲的大规模探索和殖民时代。
points.descriptionEn: On August 3, 1492, with the sponsorship of Queen Isabella I of Spain, Columbus set sail from Palos de la Frontera with three ships (the Santa María, Pinta, and Niña). After more than two months at sea, he reached an island in the Bahamas on October 12, naming it San Salvador. He mistakenly believed he had reached Asia, calling the indigenous people 'Indians.' He then explored Cuba, Haiti, and other islands, establishing the first settlement, Navidad. On March 15, 1493, he returned to Spain, reporting his discoveries to the king and queen, initiating the era of European exploration and colonization of the Americas.

points.title: 建立殖民地与统治
points.description: 1493年9月，哥伦布开始了他的第二次航行，带领17艘船和约1200人前往新发现的大陆。他在伊斯帕尼奥拉岛（今海地和多米尼加共和国）建立了第一个永久殖民地伊莎贝拉，并探索了古巴、牙买加和波多黎各等岛屿。作为殖民地的总督，哥伦布实施了对土著居民的强制劳动政策，要求他们缴纳黄金，导致大量原住民死亡。1496年，他返回西班牙，留下他的弟弟巴托洛梅奥作为总督。这一时期，哥伦布的统治方式引发了争议，但他成功地将新大陆的资源和经济潜力报告给了西班牙王室。
points.descriptionEn: In September 1493, Columbus began his second voyage, leading 17 ships and about 1,200 people to the newly discovered lands. He established the first permanent settlement, Isabella, on Hispaniola (present-day Haiti and Dominican Republic), and explored Cuba, Jamaica, and Puerto Rico. As governor of the colony, Columbus implemented policies of forced labor on indigenous peoples, requiring them to pay tribute in gold, leading to numerous deaths among the native population. In 1496, he returned to Spain, leaving his brother Bartholomeo as governor. During this period, Columbus's governance methods were controversial, but he successfully reported the resources and economic potential of the New World to the Spanish crown.

points.title: 最后一次远航与晚年
points.description: 1502年，哥伦布开始了他的第四次也是最后一次远航，探索中美洲海岸，从洪都拉斯一直航行到巴拿马。他寻找通往亚洲的海峡，但未能成功。在这次航行中，他遭遇了飓风、船只失散和与玛雅人的冲突。1504年，他返回西班牙，但此时他的声望已经下降。由于未能如预期发现大量黄金和香料，西班牙王室对他的支持减弱。1506年5月20日，哥伦布在西班牙巴利亚多利德逝世，仍然坚信他到达的是亚洲边缘。尽管如此，他的航行彻底改变了世界历史，开启了欧洲与美洲之间的持续联系，并最终导致了'哥伦布大交换'，永久改变了两个半球的人口、植物、动物和文化。
points.descriptionEn: In 1502, Columbus began his fourth and final voyage, exploring the Central American coast from Honduras to Panama. He searched for a strait to Asia but was unsuccessful. During this voyage, he encountered hurricanes, shipwrecks, and conflicts with the Maya people. In 1504, he returned to Spain, but by then his prestige had diminished. Having failed to find the expected gold and spices, support from the Spanish crown had weakened. On May 20, 1506, Columbus died in Valladolid, Spain, still believing he had reached the edge of Asia. Nevertheless, his voyages fundamentally changed world history, initiating sustained contact between Europe and the Americas and eventually leading to the 'Columbian Exchange,' which permanently altered the demographics, flora, fauna, and cultures of both hemispheres.

supporter.zh: 哥伦布被视为一位勇敢的探索者和开拓者，他的远航打破了当时人们对世界地理的认知局限，开启了全球化的序幕。支持者强调他卓越的航海技能、坚定的意志力和面对未知挑战的勇气。他的发现促进了欧洲与美洲的交流，为后来的科学探索、文化交流和经济全球化奠定了基础。从这一角度看，哥伦布代表了人类探索精神和冒险精神的典范，他的贡献远超其个人成就，对世界历史进程产生了深远影响。
supporter.en: Columbus is viewed as a courageous explorer and pioneer whose voyages broke through the geographical limitations of his time and initiated the era of globalization. Supporters emphasize his exceptional navigational skills, unwavering determination, and courage in facing the unknown. His discoveries facilitated exchange between Europe and the Americas, laying the foundation for later scientific exploration, cultural exchange, and economic globalization. From this perspective, Columbus represents the epitome of human exploration and adventurous spirit, with his impact extending far beyond personal achievements to profoundly shape the course of world history.

critic.zh: 批评者认为哥伦布的航行开启了欧洲对美洲的残酷殖民和剥削时代。他对土著居民实施了强制劳动、奴役和暴力统治，导致大量原住民死亡和文化毁灭。哥伦布的'发现'实际上是入侵，他代表了殖民主义和种族主义的早期形式。批评者指出，他的行为造成了美洲原住民人口的急剧下降，并开启了几个世纪的剥削和压迫。从这一角度看，哥伦布不应被视为英雄，而应被视为殖民主义和种族灭绝的象征人物。
critic.en: Critics argue that Columbus's voyages initiated the era of brutal European colonization and exploitation of the Americas. He implemented forced labor, enslavement, and violent rule over indigenous peoples, leading to numerous deaths and cultural destruction. Columbus's 'discovery' was essentially an invasion, representing early forms of colonialism and racism. Critics point out that his actions caused the dramatic decline of indigenous populations in the Americas and initiated centuries of exploitation and oppression. From this perspective, Columbus should not be regarded as a hero but rather as a symbolic figure of colonialism and genocide.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，哥伦布的形象经历了复杂的变化。早期他被塑造为发现新大陆的英雄，但随着后殖民主义史学的发展，他的形象变得更加复杂和矛盾。现代历史学者倾向于将哥伦布置于更广阔的历史背景中，既承认他航海成就的历史意义，也认识到其殖民行为的负面影响。在流行文化中，他既被纪念为开拓者，也被批判为殖民主义的代表。这种多元视角反映了历史评价的演变，也体现了对殖民历史更全面、批判性的理解。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Columbus's image has undergone complex transformations. Initially portrayed as the heroic discoverer of the New World, his figure has become more nuanced and contradictory with the development of postcolonial historiography. Modern historians tend to place Columbus within broader historical contexts, acknowledging both the historical significance of his navigational achievements and the negative impacts of his colonial actions. In popular culture, he is simultaneously commemorated as a pioneer and criticized as a symbol of colonialism. This multifaceted perspective reflects the evolution of historical assessment and demonstrates a more comprehensive and critical understanding of colonial history.

self.zh: 黄金、香料、珍宝和土地，这些东西可以买下世界上的一切。
self.en: Gold, spices, precious stones and other treasures are sufficient to purchase all the world's desires.

others.zh: 哥伦布的航行是人类历史上最重大的事件之一，它不仅改变了世界地图，还彻底改变了人类的历史进程。
others.en: Columbus's voyages were among the most significant events in human history, not only changing the map of the world but fundamentally altering the course of human history.

othersBy: 萨缪尔·埃利奥特·莫里森
